```shiploop-state
{
  "evidence_refs": [
    "Original request S1–S13 and intake exercise instructions",
    "README.md",
    "docs/api.md",
    "docs/operations.md",
    "docs/decisions/0006-notification-outbox.md",
    "docs/decisions/0007-append-only-audit-log.md",
    "docs/decisions/0008-json-data-file.md",
    "package.json",
    "src/app.js",
    "src/store.js",
    "src/tickets/query.js",
    "src/tickets/states.js",
    "src/outbox.js",
    "src/worker.js",
    "src/templates.js",
    "scripts/weekly-report.js",
    "test/api.test.js",
    "test/query.test.js",
    "test/service.test.js"
  ],
  "headline": "Intake established the requested outcomes, existing contract conflicts, and discovery questions; no implementation or server run was performed.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "question_categories": [
    {"id": "K1", "applies": "yes"},
    {"id": "K2", "applies": "yes"},
    {"id": "K3", "applies": "yes"},
    {"id": "K4", "applies": "yes"},
    {"id": "K5", "applies": "yes"},
    {"id": "K6", "applies": "yes"},
    {"id": "K7", "applies": "yes"},
    {"id": "K8", "applies": "yes"},
    {"id": "K9", "applies": "yes"},
    {"id": "K10", "applies": "yes"},
    {"id": "K11", "applies": "yes"},
    {"id": "K12", "applies": "yes"},
    {"id": "K13", "applies": "yes"}
  ],
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "Q1",
      "category": "K1",
      "question": "How should a requester observe a close notification, and what existing delivery boundary represents a successful heads-up?",
      "changes": "Notification content and the end-to-end acceptance check.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use the existing requester address, notification template and outbox-to-notifier path; verify the delivered notification record and its ticket information.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish the notifier and relay contract before the delivery check is specified."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q2",
      "category": "K2",
      "question": "Which existing lifecycle, API, CLI, report, persistence and notification behaviours must remain compatible?",
      "changes": "Scope and regression tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Preserve documented behaviour except the requested additions and the documented combined-filter correction; preserve weekly-report raw column positions and do not change outbox retry logic.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish current contracts before implementation choices are made."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q3",
      "category": "K3",
      "question": "What bulk-close HTTP contract supports 500 tickets, including its route, body, response, duplicate IDs, invalid IDs and mixed-state failures?",
      "changes": "Public interface, validation, atomicity and boundary tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "If discovery finds no existing contract, add a documented bulk-close endpoint accepting up to 500 ticket IDs and one X-Actor; reject an invalid batch without changing any ticket, and report a conflict for an already-closed ticket.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first establish existing routing, body limits and store transaction constraints; the exact new contract blocks implementation and client tests."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q4",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "What counts as a recent resolution heads-up, including pending, sent, failed and dead events, and which ticket and requester does suppression apply to?",
      "changes": "Deduplication rules and notification tests.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "For the same ticket and requester, suppress a close notice while its resolution notice is pending or if it was sent within the preceding five minutes; a dead notice does not suppress it. Record five minutes as an assumption, not an established policy.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the default proceeds after discovery establishes the available outbox timestamps and states."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q5",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "How are immediate delivery and anti-spam batching reconciled for single and bulk closes?",
      "changes": "Grouping, notification timing and delivery tests.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "Enqueue immediately in the close operation; for a bulk call group eligible closes by requester into one notice per requester, without a separate waiting period, and let the existing worker deliver on its next enabled tick.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the default proceeds after discovery establishes the worker and notification record constraints."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q6",
      "category": "K12",
      "question": "What is the weekly-report window: timestamp, duration, time zone and inclusive boundaries?",
      "changes": "List query contract, historical data interpretation and boundary tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "If no authoritative window is found, use a rolling seven-day UTC window ending at query time, based on the close transition time, inclusive at both ends; record that the repository's report currently counts its input rather than defining a time window.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must inspect report inputs and available close timestamps before the filter contract is finalized."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q7",
      "category": "K3",
      "question": "What list query names and validation should expose the closed-ticket window while retaining pagination and all existing filters?",
      "changes": "Endpoint contract, errors, documentation and tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Add an explicit documented recent-closed filter to GET /tickets, combine it with status and priority using AND, filter before cursor pagination, and reject invalid values with the existing 400 envelope.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must settle Q6 and inspect query and cursor behaviour before choosing the exact parameter."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q8",
      "category": "K13",
      "question": "Does idempotence require the same response on repeat close, or only the same state and side effects despite the requested 409?",
      "changes": "Repeat-close response, audit and notification tests.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "Interpret idempotence as no additional state change, audit entry or notification; return 409 conflict on a repeated close, consistent with the existing lifecycle contract.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the recorded interpretation proceeds; a person can revise it if identical responses are required."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q9",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "How are ticket, audit, notification and batch state persisted, recovered and protected from concurrent changes or partial delivery?",
      "changes": "Bulk atomicity, restart handling, duplicate prevention and recovery tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use the existing single-process store and optional atomic JSON snapshot, preserve append-only audit and existing at-least-once relay semantics, and do not promise cross-process coordination.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish persistence validation and worker interactions before a durable batching design is chosen."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q10",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "How are actors identified, what state is shared, how long does it live, and what is hidden from requesters and operators?",
      "changes": "Audit attribution, privacy expectations and interaction tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use X-Actor with the existing system fallback; tickets, audit and outbox are shared within the service and persist only when DATA_FILE is configured; send each requester only their own ticket information. Assume no new authentication, session or cross-device identity mechanism.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish the current internal API and notifier access model before specifying privacy checks."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q11",
      "category": "K6",
      "question": "Are Node, configuration, request-size and dependency constraints sufficient for the proposed 500-ticket call and running-server check?",
      "changes": "Runtime setup, validation and bulk test.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use Node 22 or later and standard-library modules only; preserve existing environment defaults and verify that the 500-ID request fits the configured body limit.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish the actual request shape and environment before the integration check."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q12",
      "category": "K7",
      "question": "Which existing store, query, worker and notifier seams can support the changes without altering outbox retry behaviour?",
      "changes": "Module boundaries and isolated tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Keep mutations and audit in the store, list parsing and filtering in the query seam, and background delivery in the existing worker; leave retry and backoff logic untouched.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must inspect persistence and delivery seams before implementation is planned."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q13",
      "category": "K8",
      "question": "Which checks prove each requested outcome at its real boundary, including a live server, 500-ticket bulk close, combined filters, deduplication, audit and restart?",
      "changes": "Exit evidence and test selection.",
      "route": "experiment",
      "default": "Run npm test and a bounded running-server integration check with controlled data and notification files; exercise positive, negative, timing-boundary, mixed-filter, repeat-close and 500-ticket cases.",
      "blocks": "The delivery loop cannot claim completion until tests and the running-server check pass; this intake is not authorized to run them."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q14",
      "category": "K9",
      "question": "Where will the changed service be delivered and what access is available for running and releasing it?",
      "changes": "Delivery and verification steps.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Deliver the reviewed changes in this repository and verify against an isolated local server in a later authorized stage; do not infer authority to deploy to a named production environment.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish the checkout and available runtime; an actual release requires an identified target and appropriate access."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q15",
      "category": "K10",
      "question": "What observable responsiveness and privacy bounds are needed beyond successful processing of 500 tickets?",
      "changes": "Performance and information-disclosure checks.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "Require a successful 500-ticket call and check for obvious pathological delays without inventing a numeric latency objective; prevent a grouped notice from exposing another requester's tickets.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the default proceeds after discovery establishes the notification and bulk contracts."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q16",
      "category": "K11",
      "question": "Can suppression, batching, persistence or retries lose a notice, duplicate side effects, expose another requester's tickets or make a bulk request partially succeed?",
      "changes": "Risk-driven design and early failure checks.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Treat these as material risks and test pending, sent, dead, restart, repeat and mixed-validity cases against the existing at-least-once delivery model.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish transaction and delivery boundaries before the risk checks are finalized."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q17",
      "category": "K12",
      "question": "How do the host's until-loop and backchain skills apply, and is an overnight Ralph loop required?",
      "changes": "Planning order, continuation condition and run cap.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use the host-listed meanings: back-chain before implementation, continue until tests and a running-server check pass, and treat Ralph-style overnight execution as optional; if used, cap it at 10 iterations or one hour, whichever comes first.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must consult the host's actual skill instructions before planning; the recorded cap applies if no stronger applicable cap is found."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q18",
      "category": "K13",
      "question": "Do the request's premises about combined filters, a weekly window and an existing bulk operation match the repository?",
      "changes": "Corrective scope, defaults and verification.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Treat combined filters as needing correction: the documented contract is AND but matchesFilters currently uses OR. The inspected weekly report defines no time window, and the inspected HTTP routes contain no bulk-close endpoint.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must check remaining repository and environment evidence before treating these findings as complete."
    }
  ],
  "summary": "S1 [fact] The target is the help desk service in this repository. S2 [outcome; assumption Q4] A close should notify the ticket's requester through the existing notification path unless a sufficiently recent resolution notice makes that redundant. S3 [outcome; assumption Q5] Enqueue promptly and group eligible bulk closes by requester to limit messages, subject to the existing worker's delivery interval. S4 [outcome; open Q6–Q7] Expose closed tickets from a weekly window; discovery must settle its meaning and query contract, with a recorded seven-day default. S5 [outcome] Combine list filters with AND as documented. S6 [fact; risk Q18] Inspection found OR in the current matcher, so the claimed existing behaviour needs correction and verification. S7 [boundary; open Q13, Q17] Back-chain before later implementation and continue an until loop until tests and a running-server check pass; this intake starts no server and implements nothing. S8 [boundary; assumption Q17] Overnight Ralph-style execution is optional and, if used, defaults to at most 10 iterations or one hour. S9 [outcome; open Q13] Use meaningful boundary tests and accurate, economical documentation. S10 [boundary] Do not change outbox retry logic; the OldTracker migration is user-provided context, not a separate task. S11 [boundary; fact] Retain the service's zero-dependency Node standard-library setup. S12 [outcome; assumption Q8] Repeated closes return 409 without further side effects, and successful closes record the X-Actor or existing system fallback. S13 [outcome; open Q3, Q11, Q15] A single bulk call must handle 500 closes, with practical responsiveness but no invented latency target. Discovery leads, not verified facts: this workspace's API, operations and decision documents, weekly-report script, store, worker, notifier, tests and host-listed skill descriptions; support leads and service operators may know the report convention, but no team channel, internal site, private repository or owner is identified. Sensitive locators belong only in an authorized private store, never committed KNOWLEDGE/. The service API is the agent entry point; requesters receive notifications, and operators inspect audit and outbox state. The request grants work in this repository, not an unspecified production deployment. An isolated run's source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return; changes become usable there after that return and in a deployed service only after release. No prior run is identified."
}
```
